chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Rib'i ibn 'Abdillah, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever seeks knowledge in order to boast before the scholars by it, or to dispute with the foolish by it, or to turn the faces of people toward him by it — let him take his seat in the Fire. Verily, leadership is not fitting except for its rightful people.

key_terms.الرِّئَاسَةَ: leadership/authority — implies both religious and worldly leadership
key_terms.السُّفَهَاءَ: the foolish/ignorant — those who lack sound judgment
key_terms.فَلْيَتَبَوَّأْ مَقْعَدَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ: let him take his seat in the Fire — a prophetic formula of warning, echoed in hadith about lying upon the Prophet
key_terms.لِأَهْلِهَا: for its rightful people — refers to those divinely qualified, namely the Imams and sincere scholars
key_terms.يُبَاهِيَ: to boast/vaunt — seeking admiration from peers by displaying knowledge
key_terms.يُمَارِيَ: to dispute/wrangle — using knowledge as a weapon in petty arguments

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about seeking knowledge for the wrong reasons?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) condemns three corrupt intentions for seeking knowledge: boasting before scholars, arguing with the ignorant, and seeking fame. This teaching was directed to a community where religious knowledge had become a social currency, and the Imam warned that misusing it for personal aggrandizement leads to hellfire. The concluding statement on leadership — that it belongs only to those truly worthy — reinforces that authority in knowledge and governance must be grounded in sincerity, not ambition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazzal Bin Shazan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who seeks the knowledge in order to boast to the scholars by it, or to argue with the fools by it, or to turn the faces of the people towards him by it, so let him assume his seat from the Fire. The leadership is not correct except for its rightful ones<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammed ibn ‘Isa from Ri’ab‘i ibn ‘Abdallah from one he narrated from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Whoever would seek knowledge to show off to the scholars or to engage in arguments with fools or to attract people to himself he should know that in so doing he has prepare his seat in the fire. Leadership does not suite anyone besides those qualified for it.”
